overview.en: This Mediterranean hawk moth is associated with pine woods.
overview.fr: Ce sphinx méditerranéen est associé aux pinèdes.

identification.en: It closely resembles Sphinx pinastri; genitalia help distinguish them.
identification.fr: Il ressemble à Sphinx pinastri ; les genitalia aident à les distinguer.

habitat.en: Its range includes North Africa, Iberia and parts of southern France.
habitat.fr: Son aire inclut l’Afrique du Nord, l’Ibérie et le sud de la France.

diet.en: Larvae feed on pines; cedar is also reported.
diet.fr: Les chenilles mangent des pins ; le cèdre est aussi signalé.

behavior.en: The two species may meet; hybrids are reported in contact zones.
behavior.fr: Les deux espèces peuvent se rencontrer ; des hybrides sont signalés en zone de contact.

reproduction.en: The consulted accounts do not establish a reliable breeding schedule.
reproduction.fr: Les sources consultées ne permettent pas d’établir un calendrier reproductif fiable.

ecology.en: See Sphinx pinastri, its similar northern relative.
ecology.fr: Voir Sphinx pinastri, son proche parent septentrional.

conservation.en: The consulted species accounts provide no global conservation rank.
conservation.fr: Les fiches consultées ne donnent pas de rang mondial de conservation.

title.en: Les Sphingidae de France — Sphinx maurorum
title.fr: Les Sphingidae de France — Sphinx maurorum

facts: The specialist French account describes its Mediterranean range, pine hosts, contact with Sphinx pinastri, hybrids, and notes that the specific phenology is not established there.

budget.method: Complete referenced bilingual sentences and factual notes.

facts: Lepinet notes similarity to Sphinx pinastri and the genital differences used for identification.
The consulted Lepinet species account does not present a global conservation rank.

budget.method: Complete referenced bilingual sentences and factual notes.

uncertainties: Distribution within France remains difficult to map because of frequent confusion with Sphinx pinastri.
No global conservation assessment was found in the consulted species references.
review_note: Concision reflects the taxonomic identification difficulty; the related pine hawkmoth is named explicitly for cross-reference.
